To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nutrition claims can affect food-related perceptions, but not necessarily food-related intake, among normal-weight and overweight/obese men and women.
nutrition claims do not affect food intake, but they do affect food perceptions.

(a) nutrition claims influence perceptions of the same food differently; (b) restrained eaters are more sensitive to the caloric content of food; and (c) overweight restrained men eat more than overweight restrained women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of nutrition labels, and the way in which these labels affect food-related perceptions, and ultimately, food intake.
the impact of healthiness of food on food-related perceptions and behavior.
the impact of nutrition labels and claims on food-related perceptions and behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nutrition claims do not seem to influence intake.
the effect of nutrition claims on intake is not straightforward, as it is dependent on the characteristics of the individual and of the food.
the effects of nutrition claims on intake are more likely to be mediated by cognitive factors, than by sensory factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
restrained men and women eat more than do unrestrained men and women when they perceive food as "healthy", and restrained overweight men eat more than do overweight men and women.
the impact of nutrition information on food-related perceptions and behaviors depends on gender, BMI, and restraint.
nutrition claims do not affect ad libitum food intake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
restrained eaters may be particularly sensitive to nutrition labels and that overweight restrained eaters may respond to nutrition claims in a way that could be detrimental to health.
the impact of nutrition labels on eating behavior may be different for men and women, as well as for people who are restrained or unrestrained in their eating.
restrained eaters, especially women, are very sensitive to the caloric content of food.
